tldr: This is a loose cluster of arXiv papers on cheaper LLM inference, not one event. It opened in late October with speculative decoding for RL rollouts and work on cutting diffusion-LM decoding rounds, then widened to pruning, MoE serving, prompt compression and drafter training.
whats_new: Overlapping Block Denoising (Nov 10) targets block-diffusion LM efficiency, the same day REAL Loss proposed training speculative-decoding drafters directly on expected acceptance length.
why_it_matters: The two lines are converging: block-diffusion models now show up as drafters inside speculative decoding, where the target model still verifies every token, which is a lower-risk route into a serving stack than replacing the autoregressive model.

beats.headline: Schedule distillation, metacognitive decoding and Measured Coupling aim to cut dLLM decoding rounds
Length extrapolation and multimodal hallucination expose weak spots
Non-diffusion-LM efficiency work shares the thread: pruning, MoE serving, compression and agent overhead
beats.summary: These papers share the efficient-inference theme, not the diffusion-LM method; one is an image-diffusion privacy paper matched on the word alone.

beats.headline: Speculative decoding papers chase longer accepted drafts
beats.summary: Two papers a few days apart, D-REAL and REAL Loss, both train the drafter on acceptance length instead of token-level loss.

beats.headline: Block-diffusion drafters enter speculative decoding
beats.summary: D3Tree and DForkTree treat a block-diffusion model as the drafter and work on the draft tree the target verifies.

beats.headline: Block diffusion LMs get their own inference optimizations

open_questions: Do the schedule-distillation, metacognitive-decoding, Measured Coupling and SpecCTMC speedups hold on independent benchmarks at equal output quality?
Does any inference framework or vendor ship diffusion LLM serving with parallel decoding?
Does RangeSWA's training-free extrapolation hold on long outputs beyond the paper's tested lengths?
Does a block-diffusion drafter with a pruned draft tree beat existing drafters on end-to-end throughput under concurrent serving load?
Do D-REAL and REAL Loss report comparable acceptance-length gains on the same drafter and target pairs?
take_for_builders: Do not plan serving capacity around diffusion LLMs yet. If you run speculative decoding, the nearer-term experiment is a block-diffusion drafter: measure accepted length and verification cost under your real concurrency before adopting it.
